question: How was Iltutmish related to Qutubuddin Aibak?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Son-in-law**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Qutubuddin Aibak was a slave of Muhammad Ghori.
 
• He was later appointed as the Viceroy of Muhammad Ghori's Indian territories.
 
• After Muhammad Ghori's death, Qutubuddin Aibak founded the Mamluk Dynasty in India, also known as the Slave Dynasty.
 
• He was a key figure in the establishment of Muslim rule in India, laying the foundation for subsequent dynasties.
 
• Qutubuddin Aibak was known for his architectural contributions, including the construction of the Qutub Minar in Delhi.
 
• He was succeeded by his son-in-law Iltutmish, who further consolidated the Sultanate of Delhi.
 
• Qutubuddin Aibak's reign marked the beginning of a new era in Indian history, characterized by the establishment of Muslim governance in Northern India.
 
• The Slave Dynasty ruled from 1206 to 1290 and was succeeded by the Khalji Dynasty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Shamsuddin Iltutmish (1211-36 AD) was the first Ilbari ruler.
 
• Iltutmish is considered the real founder of the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• At the time of Qutbuddin Aibak's death, he was the governor of Badaun.
 
• Aibuq had made Iltutmish the Iqtedar (Subedar) of Badaun.
 
• The nobles of Delhi, especially Shah Ismail, invited Iltutmish, the governor of Badaun, to sit on the throne of Delhi, which he immediately accepted.
 
• In June 1211, Iltutmish became the Sultan by defeating Aramshah and the rebels in the field of Jud (Bagh-i-Jud).
 
• 
 
First of all, Dr. Arnold expressed the opinion that 'Iltutmish was the usurper of the throne of Delhi.'
